_comment: Copy this file to configs/bots.json (which is git-ignored) and fill in real values.
The server reloads bots.json every 30 s, so you can update bot tokens or usernames
without a full container restart — just edit the file and the new values take effect.
bot_index   : integer index matching the /webhook/{bot_index} path (0 = /webhook)
bot_username: Telegram @username (without @), used for logging and file-ID routing
secret_token: the X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token expected in each webhook POST.
If omitted or null the server falls back to the runtime-generated token.
Update procedure when a bot is replaced / redeployed:
1. Create a new bot via @BotFather and note the new token.
2. Run setup_webhooks.py (or call setWebhook manually) with the new token.
Pass a stable secret_token you choose (e.g. openssl rand -hex 32).
3. Update the matching entry in configs/bots.json with the new secret_token.
4. Within ~30 s the server picks up the new token — no restart required.
